decoder_context: Matrix is the finite real matrix algebra on the displayed index set. Matrix multiplication is ordinary algebra multiplication, scalar multiplication is real scalar multiplication, and 1 is the identity matrix.

For a real square matrix, IsHermitian means that its transpose equals itself. PosSemidef means positive semidefinite in the full quadratic-form sense, including self-adjointness; it is not an entrywise inequality.
NormedSpace.exp on this real matrix algebra is its convergent matrix power-series exponential. It is not the entrywise real exponential. Real.exp is the scalar real exponential.
The active matrix norm is the Euclidean L2 operator norm, with the ordinary finite-coordinate topology. The scalar real matrix algebra and rational-algebra structure are the standard ones.
Fin n is the finite set of natural numbers strictly less than n; i.val is its zero-based natural index. Natural numbers embed into real numbers in the usual way.

EuclideanSpace real (Fin n) is real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its Euclidean norm and Borel structure. WithLp.toLp 2 wraps coordinates as a Euclidean vector, and WithLp.ofLp recovers the same coordinates.

stdGaussian is the centered Gaussian probability measure with identity covariance. Measure.pi is the displayed finite product measure on the function space. A measure in a displayed integral is exactly that measure, without implicit conditioning.

Real.log is the natural logarithm and Real.sqrt is the nonnegative real square root. An if-test written with less-than-or-equal includes equality. Real inverses are totalized at zero in the usual field convention.
Matrix.vecMulVec u v has entry u_i v_j. The Kronecker product has entry A_(i,k) B_(j,l) at row (i,j) and column (k,l); the paired indices preserve this displayed order.

The displayed integrals are Bochner integrals in the corresponding finite matrix space. Their definition is totalized to zero for a nonintegrable integrand. Reconstruct the displayed proposition without adding integrability premises or conclusions.

/-! Real matrix exponential estimates for the deterministic step of Tropp's
bounded Bernstein MGF argument (author preprint, Lemma 6.7, pp. 25–26).
The actual Gaussian single-summand consumer has its own original probability law.
-/

open MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators Matrix.Norms.L2Operator

noncomputable section

universe u

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.MatrixBernsteinExponential

private lemma exponential_remainder_integral (k : ℝ) :
    Real.exp k - 1 - k =
      k ^ 2 * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, (1 - t) * Real.exp (k * t) := by
  have hd : ∀ t : ℝ,
      HasDerivAt (fun u : ℝ => Real.exp (k * u)) (k * Real.exp (k * t)) t := by
    intro t
    exact ((hasDerivAt_const_mul k (x := t)).exp).congr_deriv (mul_comm _ _)
  have hv : ∀ t : ℝ,
      HasDerivAt (fun u : ℝ => k * Real.exp (k * u))
        (k ^ 2 * Real.exp (k * t)) t := by
    intro t
    exact (hd t).const_mul k |>.congr_deriv (by ring)
  have hke : IntervalIntegrable (fun t : ℝ => k * Real.exp (k * t)) volume 0 1 :=
    (by fun_prop : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => k * Real.exp (k * t))).intervalIntegrable _ _
  have he : (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, k * Real.exp (k * t)) = Real.exp k - 1 := by
    simpa only [mul_one, mul_zero, Real.exp_zero] using
      intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt (fun t _ => hd t) hke
  have hp := intervalIntegral.integral_mul_deriv_eq_deriv_mul_of_hasDerivAt
    (u := fun t : ℝ => 1 - t) (v := fun t : ℝ => k * Real.exp (k * t))
    (u' := fun _ : ℝ => -1) (v' := fun t : ℝ => k ^ 2 * Real.exp (k * t))
    (a := (0 : ℝ)) (b := 1)
    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
    (fun t _ => ((hasDerivAt_const t (1 : ℝ)).sub (hasDerivAt_id t)).congr_deriv (by ring))
    (fun t _ => hv t)
    ((by fun_prop : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => (-1 : ℝ))).intervalIntegrable _ _)
    ((by fun_prop : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => k ^ 2 * Real.exp (k * t))).intervalIntegrable _ _)
  have hfactor :
      (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, (1 - t) * (k ^ 2 * Real.exp (k * t))) =
        k ^ 2 * ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, (1 - t) * Real.exp (k * t) := by
    calc
      _ = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, k ^ 2 * ((1 - t) * Real.exp (k * t)) :=
        intervalIntegral.integral_congr (fun t _ => by ring)
      _ = _ := intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul _ _
  rw [hfactor] at hp
  simp only [sub_self, zero_mul, sub_zero, mul_zero, Real.exp_zero, mul_one, one_mul,
    neg_one_mul, intervalIntegral.integral_neg, he] at hp
  linarith

private def remainderKernel (k : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, (1 - t) * Real.exp (k * t)

private lemma remainderKernel_monotone : Monotone remainderKernel := by
  intro x y hxy
  unfold remainderKernel
  apply intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on zero_le_one
    ((by fun_prop : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => (1 - t) * Real.exp (x * t))).intervalIntegrable _ _)
    ((by fun_prop : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => (1 - t) * Real.exp (y * t))).intervalIntegrable _ _)
  intro t ht
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hxy ht.1)) (sub_nonneg.mpr ht.2)

private lemma remainderKernel_zero : remainderKernel 0 = 1 / 2 := by
  simp only [remainderKernel, zero_mul, Real.exp_zero, mul_one]
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_sub]
  · norm_num [intervalIntegral.integral_const, integral_id]
  · exact continuous_const.intervalIntegrable _ _
  · exact continuous_id.intervalIntegrable _ _

private def bernsteinRemainder (s x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if x = 0 then s ^ 2 / 2 else (Real.exp (s * x) - s * x - 1) / x ^ 2

private lemma bernsteinRemainder_eq_kernel (s x : ℝ) :
    bernsteinRemainder s x = s ^ 2 * remainderKernel (s * x) := by
  by_cases hx : x = 0
  · subst x
    simp [bernsteinRemainder, remainderKernel_zero, div_eq_mul_inv]
  · rw [bernsteinRemainder, if_neg hx]
    apply (div_eq_iff (pow_ne_zero 2 hx)).2
    calc
      Real.exp (s * x) - s * x - 1 = Real.exp (s * x) - 1 - s * x := by ring
      _ = (s * x) ^ 2 * remainderKernel (s * x) := exponential_remainder_integral _
      _ = (s ^ 2 * remainderKernel (s * x)) * x ^ 2 := by ring

private lemma bernsteinRemainder_monotone {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    Monotone (bernsteinRemainder s) := by
  intro x y hxy
  rw [bernsteinRemainder_eq_kernel, bernsteinRemainder_eq_kernel]
  exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
    (remainderKernel_monotone (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hxy hs.le)) (sq_nonneg s)

private lemma bernsteinRemainder_mul_sq (s x : ℝ) :
    bernsteinRemainder s x * x ^ 2 = Real.exp (s * x) - s * x - 1 := by
  by_cases hx : x = 0
  · subst x
    simp [bernsteinRemainder]
  · rw [bernsteinRemainder, if_neg hx]
    field_simp

private lemma bernstein_scalar_bound {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) {x : ℝ} (hx : x ≤ 1) :
    Real.exp (s * x) ≤ 1 + s * x + (Real.exp s - s - 1) * x ^ 2 := by
  have hone : bernsteinRemainder s 1 = Real.exp s - s - 1 := by
    simp [bernsteinRemainder]
  have h := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (bernsteinRemainder_monotone hs hx) (sq_nonneg x)
  rw [bernsteinRemainder_mul_sq, hone] at h
  linarith

/-- The deterministic real-matrix inequality in the proof of Tropp's Lemma 6.7.
The upper spectral cap is one-sided; negative eigenvalues are unrestricted. -/
theorem bernstein_exponential_quadratic_bound
    {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (hA : A.IsHermitian)
    (hA_le : (1 - A).PosSemidef) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 < s) :
    ((1 : Matrix ι ι ℝ) + s • A + (Real.exp s - s - 1) • (A * A) -
      NormedSpace.exp (s • A)).PosSemidef := by
  have hSA : IsSelfAdjoint A := hA.isSelfAdjoint
  have hle : A ≤ 1 := Matrix.le_iff.mpr hA_le
  have hspec : ∀ x ∈ spectrum ℝ A, x ≤ 1 :=
    (CFC.le_one_iff (R := ℝ) A hSA).mp hle
  have hfc : cfc (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) A ≤
      cfc (fun x : ℝ => 1 + s * x + (Real.exp s - s - 1) * (x * x)) A := by
    exact cfc_mono (a := A)
      (fun x hx => by simpa only [pow_two] using bernstein_scalar_bound hs (hspec x hx))
      (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
  have hleft : cfc (fun x : ℝ => Real.exp (s * x)) A = NormedSpace.exp (s • A) := by
    calc
      _ = cfc Real.exp (s • A) := cfc_comp_const_mul s Real.exp A (by fun_prop) hSA
      _ = _ := CFC.real_exp_eq_normedSpace_exp ((IsSelfAdjoint.all s).smul hSA)
  have hright :
      cfc (fun x : ℝ => 1 + s * x + (Real.exp s - s - 1) * (x * x)) A =
        (1 : Matrix ι ι ℝ) + s • A + (Real.exp s - s - 1) • (A * A) := by
    rw [cfc_add (a := A) (fun x : ℝ => 1 + s * x)
        (fun x : ℝ => (Real.exp s - s - 1) * (x * x)) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop),
      cfc_add (a := A) (fun _ : ℝ => 1) (fun x : ℝ => s * x) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop),
      cfc_const (R := ℝ) 1 A hSA,
      cfc_const_mul_id s A hSA,
      cfc_const_mul (Real.exp s - s - 1) (fun x : ℝ => x * x) A (by fun_prop),
      cfc_mul (fun x : ℝ => x) (fun x : ℝ => x) A (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop),
      cfc_id' ℝ A hSA, map_one]
  exact Matrix.le_iff.mp (by simpa only [hleft, hright] using hfc)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.MatrixBernsteinExponential

private lemma exp_sub_one_add_posSemidef
    {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (A : Matrix ι ι ℝ) (hA : A.IsHermitian) :
    (NormedSpace.exp A - (1 + A)).PosSemidef := by
  have hSA : IsSelfAdjoint A := hA.isSelfAdjoint
  have hfc : cfc (fun x : ℝ => 1 + x) A ≤ cfc Real.exp A :=
    cfc_mono (a := A) (fun x _ => by linarith [Real.add_one_le_exp x])
      (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
  have hlin : cfc (fun x : ℝ => 1 + x) A = (1 : Matrix ι ι ℝ) + A := by
    rw [cfc_add (a := A) (fun _ : ℝ => 1) (fun x : ℝ => x) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop),
      cfc_const (R := ℝ) 1 A hSA, cfc_id' ℝ A hSA, map_one]
  exact Matrix.le_iff.mp
    (by simpa only [hlin, CFC.real_exp_eq_normedSpace_exp hSA] using hfc)

For every pair \(d,q\in\mathbb N=\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\) satisfying
\[
2q+1<d,
\]
make the following definitions, all of which remain in scope for the entire subsequent proposition. Write
\[
I=\{0,\ldots,d-1\},\qquad J=\{0,\ldots,q\},
\]
with the zero-based indices shown, and set
\[
D=\mathbb R^I,\qquad E=\mathbb R^J,\qquad
\Omega=\{\omega:J\to D\}.
\]
The spaces \(D\) and \(E\) have their Euclidean norms and Borel structures. Let \(\gamma_D\) be the centered Gaussian probability measure on \(D\) with identity covariance, and define the finite product measure
\[
\mu=\bigotimes_{b\in J}\gamma_D
\quad\text{on }\Omega.
\]
Define the real scalars
\[
r=q+1,\qquad L=2r+3\log(1000d),
\]
where the natural numbers in these real expressions are embedded into \(\mathbb R\), and \(\log\) is the natural logarithm. For \(i\in I\) and \(k\in J\), put
\[
\theta_i=\frac{(i+1-\tfrac12)\pi}{d},
\qquad
t_i(k)=
\begin{cases}
1,&k=0,\\
\sqrt{2}\cos(k\theta_i),&k\ne0.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\sqrt{2}\) is the nonnegative real square root. For \(i\in I\) and \(\omega\in\Omega\), let
\[
u_i(\omega)=\bigl(\omega(b)(i)\bigr)_{b\in J}\in E,
\qquad
\|u_i(\omega)\|_2^2=\sum_{b\in J}\omega(b)(i)^2.
\]
Let \(\operatorname{Mat}_{J\times J}(\mathbb R)\) denote the real square matrices whose rows and columns are indexed by the ordered pairs in \(J\times J\). Define
\[
Y_i(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
d^{-1}\bigl(u_i(\omega)u_i(\omega)^{\mathsf T}\bigr)
\otimes\bigl(t_i t_i^{\mathsf T}\bigr),
&\|u_i(\omega)\|_2^2\le L,\\
0,&\|u_i(\omega)\|_2^2>L,
\end{cases}
\]
as an element of \(\operatorname{Mat}_{J\times J}(\mathbb R)\). The equality case belongs to the first branch. The outer products use the displayed real coordinates. In the Kronecker product, the row pair is \((b,k)\) and the column pair is \((c,\ell)\); consequently its entry in the first branch is exactly
\[
\bigl(Y_i(\omega)\bigr)_{(b,k),(c,\ell)}
=d^{-1}\,\omega(b)(i)\,\omega(c)(i)\,t_i(k)\,t_i(\ell)
\qquad (b,k,c,\ell\in J).
\]
Next define, for every \(i\in I\),
\[
\operatorname{mean}_i=\int_{\Omega}Y_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega),
\qquad
Z_i(\omega)=Y_i(\omega)-\operatorname{mean}_i,
\]
and put
\[
\rho=\frac{2r(L+1)}{d},
\qquad
X_i(\omega)=\rho^{-1}Z_i(\omega).
\]
All scalar inverses and divisions use the real-field convention in which the inverse of zero is zero.

Then, for every real \(s\) satisfying \(0<s\), and then for every \(i\in I\),
\[
\exp\!\left((e^s-s-1)
       \int_{\Omega}X_i(\omega)X_i(\omega)\,d\mu(\omega)\right)
-
\int_{\Omega}\exp\!\bigl(sX_i(\omega)\bigr)\,d\mu(\omega)
\succeq0.
\]

All displayed integrals are Bochner integrals in the indicated finite real matrix space, taken with respect to exactly \(\mu\), with no conditioning; by their definition an integral is zero when its integrand is not integrable. No integrability premise or conclusion is added to this proposition. Matrix products are ordinary matrix products, and scalar multiples are real scalar multiples. For \(M\in\operatorname{Mat}_{J\times J}(\mathbb R)\), the relation \(M\succeq0\) means \(M^{\mathsf T}=M\) and \(v^{\mathsf T}Mv\ge0\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^{J\times J}\). The matrix exponential is the convergent algebra power series
\[
\exp(M)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{M^n}{n!},
\qquad M^0=I_{J\times J},
\]
using the Euclidean \(L^2\) operator norm and ordinary finite-coordinate topology, while \(e^s\) is the scalar real exponential. The allowed boundary cases are exactly those specified by \(d,q\in\mathbb N\) and \(2q+1<d\); in particular \(q=0\) is allowed, while these conditions make \(I\) and \(J\) nonempty.
